content:
@Yaël Dillies  and I have just finished the first in a series of three blog posts about simprocs: Simprocs for the Working Mathematician.

This gives a beginner-friendly introduction to what simprocs are, and how one can use them. The subsequent posts will give a more detailed description of the internals of the simp tactic and show how Lean users can go about writing their own simprocs.

Feel free to suggest topics that you would like us to discuss in the next posts - discussion thread here: #general > Discussion: Simproc blog post
We'd also like to thank everyone who reviewed the drafts and suggested improvements!

The second simprocs blog post is now out: Simp, made simple.

This gives a more in-depth description of the inner workings of the simp tactic, and sets the scene for the third blog post, where we will walk readers through the process of writing their own simprocs.

If you have suggestions or things you would like us to cover in the final post, feel free to add those in the discussion thread: #general > Discussion: Simproc blog post.

Finally, a big thanks to @Anne Baanen and all the other reviewers who suggested improvements to the initial drafts!

The third and final simprocs blog post is now out: Fantastic Simprocs and How to Write Them!

Following the previous post that gave some details about the inner workings of the simp tactic, this one walks the reader through the process of implementing a simproc for a concrete problem.

Comments, corrections & co are very welcome in the discussion thread: #general > Discussion: Simproc blog post.

Thanks again to @Anne Baanen for all the reviews and help getting this out:)
